section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Sages' analogy of "scent" versus "oil" in Shir HaShirim reveals the three innovations of the Giving of the Torah: the essence (Atzmus) was drawn into Torah and mitzvos.
section.t: And this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said
on the verse
"For the scent of your good oils, your name is like poured oil,"
"All the songs
that the Patriarchs said before You were [mere] scents, but we [have] 'your name is like poured oil,' like a person who pours from vessel to vessel."
"All the mitzvos that the Patriarchs performed before You were [mere] scents, but we [have] 'your name is like poured oil.'"
One can say
that in this statement of our Sages, all three matters that were innovated at the Giving of the Torah are explained.
For the difference between scent and oil in themselves—
that scent is only an expansion
(an illumination)
of the oil—
indicates the innovation in Torah and mitzvos
(that were given at the Giving of the Torah)
regarding the Giver of the Torah and the Commander of the mitzvos.
For the Torah as it is in itself
(the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He)
is only an illumination
(a scent),
and the true essence of the matter that "the Torah and the Holy One, blessed be He, are entirely one"
was actualized at the Giving of the Torah,
for then the Awtsmoos
(oil) was drawn into it.
And likewise regarding the mitzvos,
that at the Giving of the Torah the Awtsmoos was drawn into them.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section details two further distinctions between scent and oil: oil is diminished when poured, unlike scent, and oil is absorbed and transforms the body permanently, unlike scent which dissipates.
section.t: And there is another difference between the scent of the oil and the oil itself:
that by smelling the scent of the oil, nothing is lacking from the oil,
but not so when one takes the oil itself, it is diminished in the place where it was initially
("your name is like poured oil,"
like a person who pours from vessel to vessel).
And in the allegory, this is:
that by the giving of the Torah below,
the power to adjudicate law was taken
from the supernal beings,
for "the Torah is not
in heaven."
And yet another difference between scent and oil:
that the scent goes and is consumed until nothing remains of it,
and also the pleasure that a person derives from the scent,
after the scent ceases, his pleasure passes,
but not so food
(oil),
for even after the food is digested in his intestines,
it remains in existence,
except that it is transformed into blood and flesh,
and thereby it affects the person so that his characteristics become like the characteristics of the food.
And in the allegory, this is:
that the drawing down through the fulfillment of mitzvos, and all the more so through the study of Torah by the Patriarchs, was not fixed in the world in its inwardness.
But through the study of Torah after the Giving of the Torah, and all the more so through the fulfillment of mitzvos, a change in the world is effected inwardly and permanently.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the primary innovation at Sinai was the drawing of Awtsmoos into Torah, which then empowered Torah and mitzvos to change the world and gave Israel the power to rule on law.
section.t: And one can say
that regarding the three matters mentioned above that were innovated at the Giving of the Torah,
the primary innovation is that at the Giving of the Torah the drawing of the Awtsmoos into the Torah was effected,
and through this the innovation was also effected in the Torah and in the recipients of the Torah.
For the Torah in itself,
since it is utterly incomparable to the world,
there is no change in the things of the world through the laws of the Torah,
and likewise regarding the mitzvos.

And the power in the Torah and mitzvos that were given at the Giving of the Torah to effect change in the world is because at the Giving of the Torah the Awtsmoos was drawn into the Torah and its mitzvos,
and through this they have the power to effect change even in the things of the world that are not comparable to Torah and mitzvos, for the Awtsmoos is in every place.
And likewise regarding the power given to Yisrael to adjudicate halachos, even to the level of "the Holy One, blessed be He, said 'My children have defeated Me, My children have defeated Me,'"
for this power in Yisrael is because the root of the souls is in His Essence, may He be blessed,
(above the manner in which He contracted Himself into the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He).
And the revelation of the root of the soul
(as it is rooted in the Awtsmoos)
in the soul as it comes in a chain of descent, and all the more so in the soul clothed in the body,
is through the Torah.
For since the opening of the Giving of the Torah was with "Anochi," an acronym for "Ana Nafshi Ketavit Yehavit" (I wrote and gave over My very Self),
that He, as it were, inserted His Essence into the Torah,
through this it was effected that "Anochi"
(Hashem)
"your G-d"
(in the singular)
[is the G-d] of each and every individual of Yisrael,
and through his proper engagement with the Torah,
this is drawn into revelation.
